The fair value of the Front Line Care reporting unit was determined based on a discounted cash flow model (an income approach) and earnings multiples (a market approach) based on the guideline public company method. Significant assumptions used in the determination of the fair values of our reporting units generally include revenue growth rates, forecasted earnings before income, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) margins, discount rates, terminal growth rates and earnings multiples. The discounted cash flow model used to determine the fair value of our Front Line Care reporting unit reflected our most recent cash flow projections, a discount rate of 9.5% and a terminal growth rate of 3.25%. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

We rely on patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, know-how and confidentiality agreements to develop, maintain and strengthen our competitive position.
Products manufactured by us are sold primarily under our own trademarks and trade names.
Our continued success depends upon the quality of our products.
Our ability to achieve these anticipated benefits also depends on factors over which we may have limited control, including competitive pressures and evolving regulatory requirements.
In certain instances, we use a single source or supplier or there is only a sole source or supplier.
Our reliance on sole source suppliers may also lead to increased costs.
Additionally, our success depends upon the availability and quality of our products and the underlying raw materials and component parts.
Our success also depends on our ability to maintain and routinely improve product quality and our quality management program.

We rely upon information technology systems (IT systems) and infrastructure, including services provided by our partners and third parties, to support our business, facilities, operations, product development, products, and services.

We also routinely rely on technology systems and infrastructure in the collection, use, storage and transfer, disclosure, and other processing of voluminous amounts of protected information, including personal data, protected health information, and sensitive data (of patients, employees, customers, and third parties) as well as internal confidential information (collectively, Protected Information).

Third-party systems and solutions that we rely on are also vulnerable to the same risks and may contain defects in design or manufacture or other problems that could result in system disruption or compromise the information security of our own systems, products, and services.

Additionally, our ongoing integration of Hillrom and the sale of our Kidney Care business, as well as a number of our employees having fully remote or hybrid work arrangements expose us to, among other things, heightened risks related to our information technology systems and networks, including cyber attacks, computer viruses, malicious software, security breaches and telecommunication failures, both for systems and networks we control directly and for those that employees and third-party developers rely on to work remotely.

The ultimate impact of any tariffs and any retaliatory counter measures will depend on various factors, including if any tariffs are ultimately implemented, the timing of implementation, the amount, scope and nature of the tariffs, and the applicability of such tariffs to Baxter’s product portfolio.
We also rely on trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets and know-how to develop, maintain and strengthen our competitive positions.

The timing, declaration, amount, and payment of any future dividends fall within the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on many factors, including our available cash, estimated cash needs, earnings, financial condition, operating results, capital requirements, limitations in our contractual agreements, applicable law, regulatory constraints, industry practice, and other business considerations that our Board of Directors considers relevant.
Sole source supplier relationships may limit our ability to respond to these tariffs with alternative or lower cost raw materials or component parts.
Realization of the U.S. and foreign operating loss and tax credit carryforwards depends on generating sufficient future earnings.
